answer: Tie identity to a comet that passes only once: each account must solve a fresh puzzle seeded by unpredictable public randomness, so a precomputed Sybil army expires before it can act. Grow a yarrow bed of slow trust: rights accumulate only through months of small, distinct, publicly useful contributions, and any sudden burst of activity resets the clock. At the zenith, standing is the product of independent long-lived relationships, not a count of accounts, so cloning buys nothing a patient honest user cannot earn for free. All steps are logged publicly, so auditors can replay any climb.
